hyps.why: Lowering an excessively high learning rate rescues training, whereas at low lr it does little.
Raising an already large learning rate destabilizes training.
Deeper networks diverge more easily with large learning rates.
More L2 on an already heavily regularized model causes underfitting.
Relaxing heavy regularization restores capacity and accuracy.
Narrower networks are more stable under large learning rates.
A very small learning rate undertrains in a fixed epoch budget, so increasing it helps.
Going from one layer to two or more is more harmful in the sampled regimes than going deeper from two layers.
Smaller batches add gradient noise that compounds with a large learning rate.
With a slow learning rate, extra width speeds effective learning and improves accuracy.
